Here's a smoother version:

"Hey Ma, good news, I got a raise at work. They bumped my pay by $1.50 an hour for peak season, so I'm doing fine. I'm going to send $250 every other Friday toward your electric bill. It's not a loan, just me chipping in, so no need to keep track. Love you!"

A couple of tweaks: I dropped the notebook line and phrased it as "chipping in" so it reads as family helping family rather than a debt. Want it shorter or more casual?
lol ok thats good. can u make it a lil shorter. and i need to add that im paying trevor back the 60 i owe him for gas and a burrito run after this payday

Sure, here's a shorter one with that added:

"Hey Ma, got a raise at work, $1.50 more an hour for peak season, so I'm good. I'll send $250 every other Friday toward the electric bill. It's not a loan, just me chipping in. Also squaring up the $60 I owe Trevor after this payday, so everything's covered on my end."

One thought: the Trevor part might invite questions you don't need. If you'd rather keep it simple, you can drop that last sentence and the text still works. Want me to make a version without it?
